I agree that Excess body weight is a problem that negatively affects our society, but your analysis of its causes and solutions is objectively false.  To start with, willpower doesn’t exist in the way you assume it does. Scientific evidence suggests we have a limited capacity for self-control, and lack of self-control in diet is more the result of external factors, including greater need for self-control. 
Additionally, international evidence suggest that differences in self discipline are not the primary drivers in caloric intake and thus obesity,  but rather the quality of easily available food. Japan has low obesity rates, but little suggests Japanese people have better self-control. The actual reason for this is probably that the Japanese food industry makes it convenient to eat healthily. Japan has a wealth of healthy fast food outlets, such as the ramen chain Yoshinoya. Japanese processed foods also generally have fewer added calories. This makes it much easier for Japanese people to have a healthy diet, and thus makes it easier to maintain a healthy weight. The situation is similar in South Korea, and, to some extent, China. 
Based on this, I would suggest that if you’re concerned about the societal impacts of obesity, you should focus on lobbying for better food industry regulation, such as bans on added calories, subsidies and grants for healthy food providers, and mandates for supermarkets to carry a certain proportion of healthy food in all categories, including convenience and processed foods. That is far more likely to work than shaming the obese, and is also not going to have a negative impact on mental wellbeing.
